hits.title: Tropic names co-founder Justin Etkin CEO as AI procurement business expands
hits.snippet: Tropic has named co-founder Justin Etkin as CEO, formalizing a leadership transition at the New York-based procurement technology company as it expands its AI-powered spend intelligence platform for enterprise software buyers. The change, announced August 13, 2026, comes as the company reports a 79% year-over-year increase in bookings and manages more than $23 billion in customer spending. Co-founder David Campbell, who led Tropic since its founding, will remain chairman of the board and an active advisor, focusing on go-to-market strategy and corporate initiatives. Etkin, previously Chief Operating Officer, takes responsibility for the company's next stage of growth. The succession follows Tropic's shift from a services-led procurement business toward a software and intelligence platform designed to help finance and procurement teams manage increasingly complex software and AI portfolios. ## Founders split responsibilities Campbell helped oversee the transition while building the executive team that will support the company's next phase. hits.title: Tropic Cinema Begins New Chapter Under PACKW | How the Community Can Help
hits.snippet: # A New Chapter for Tropic Cinema: Community Support Will Help Shape Its Future August 05, 2026 • Key West Tourist Key West has long been a place where creativity thrives. From the literary legacy of Tennessee Williams and Ernest Hemingway to generations of musicians, actors, filmmakers, painters, and storytellers, the island has earned a reputation as one of America's most vibrant arts communities. That creative tradition is entering an important new chapter. On August 4, 2026, Performing Arts Centers of Key West (PACKW) officially assumed responsibility for operating Tropic Cinema. The organization, which already manages the historic Tennessee Williams Theatre and the KeysTix ticketing platform, announced that it will oversee the cinema's daily operations while preserving its mission of bringing independent, documentary, foreign, and thought-provoking films to Key West audiences. For nearly three decades, the Key West Film Society built Tropic Cinema into far more than a movie theater.
